subject: Sustained QPS gating and warmup checkpoint for private GPU pool
messages:
From: Anna Torres <anna@nebulahealth.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 20 Aug 2026 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Private deployment throughput baseline and warmup questions

Hi Jonas / Laura,

Thanks for the walkthrough yesterday. Before we lock in the Dedicated/Private contract, our infra team asked for a concrete throughput commitment and warmup expectations for the Nebula on-prem GPU cluster:

- Average sustained inference workload: ~4,000 qps (chat-style requests), average prompt + response token length ~600 tokens.
- Target p99 latency: < 350ms for standard chat route.
- Warmup window: how long to reach steady-state performance after pool spin-up or network flap?
- Network egress estimate for peak sustained load (we need these numbers for firewall/NAT sizing).

Could you share a recommended capacity floor, admission-control gating thresholds, and a warmup plan (including cache prewarming steps)? Procurement also needs an estimate of how many GPUs we'd reserve for the first 12 months.

Attaching our rough traffic samples.

Thanks,
Anna

--
Anna Torres
CTO, Nebula Health
anna@nebulahealth.com
From: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
To: Anna Torres <anna@nebulahealth.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 20 Aug 2026 11:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Private deployment throughput baseline and warmup questions

Hi Anna — thanks for the details and the sample traces.

Short answers up-front:
- Recommended capacity floor: reserve to support 1.5x your sustained qps = ~6k qps headroom. With our quantized LLM profile for your model family that maps to ~24 A100-equivalent vGPUs for sustained traffic (conservative). We'll provide a line-itemized mapping in the attached capacity-model-v2.xlsx.
- Admission-control gating: two layers — soft gate at 85% pool utilisation (requests receive slower retry hints), hard gate at 95% (reject with 503 + Retry-After). We'll document token- and request-level thresholds.
- Warmup: cache/KV prewarm achieves ~80% steady-state hit rate within 8–12 minutes for representative traffic; full plateau (max KV priming + kernel JITs) at ~30 minutes after cold start. We recommend keeping a minimal warm pool (2–3 GPUs) warm during maintenance windows.
- Network egress: estimate attached; for your average payloads and 4k qps it's ~2.8 Gbps outbound (including overheads). Please confirm your NAT/egress sizing requirements.

Next steps: Laura and I will follow up with a mutual action plan and procurement-ready numbers. See attached capacity-model-v2.xlsx and network-egress-matrix.pdf.

Best,

Jonas Weber
Principal Infra PM
Redwood Inference
jonas_weber@redwood.com
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>

Date: Fri, 21 Aug 2026 08:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Private deployment throughput baseline and warmup questions

Adding a few ops/implementation notes on the warmup and gating approach:

- Prefix/KV cache: we recommend a two-pass warmup. First pass: synthetic workload that mirrors your token lengths (we can run this remotely during provisioning). Second pass: traffic-driven ramp (we'll route a small percentage of production traffic through a warm pool to accelerate hit-rate).
- Admission control parameters we propose to expose: max_tokens_per_minute_per_conn, token_rate_soft_threshold, token_rate_hard_threshold, per-route QPS caps. These are adjustable via the Private control plane.
- Failure modes: on cross-region egress outages we will failover to a lower-capacity compatible model (quantized 4-bit variant) to preserve availability while shedding cost/latency.
- Observability hooks: pre-warm status, cache hit curves, and per-GPU util metrics will be shipped to your monitoring endpoints (Prometheus pushgateway or our pull endpoint).

Let us know if Nebula's infra team prefers that we provide the synthetic warmup artifact as a runnable container image or a script.

-Vivek

3) Week 4: Gradual traffic ramp to production (canary -> 25% -> 50% -> 100%)
